paragraphs: Here's the lesson, friend. Rehoboam's kingdom was steady, his power was established, and that's exactly when he and all Israel "forsook the Law of the LORD" (2 Chronicles 12:1). Strong times can be the riskiest times, because that's when we stop leaning. I've seen it in my own bakery: the batch is going great, and that's the moment I quit watching the oven.

Now look at what turned things around. When Shemaiah the prophet brought the LORD's word, the king and the leaders said, "The LORD is righteous" (2 Chronicles 12:6). They didn't argue, hide or make excuses. And "When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves," He said, "I will not destroy them" (2 Chronicles 12:7). Humility got there before the rescue did, friend.

But hold on, because the ending is honest. Rehoboam humbled himself, and the LORD's anger turned away, yet the writer still says he "did evil because he did not set his heart to seek the LORD" (2 Chronicles 12:14). One good moment of bowing low isn't the same as a heart that keeps seeking. So the question for you, baker, is simple: will you seek Him in the steady days too? That's the heart my ovens stay ready with, and this story, the last one in Rehoboam's reign, shows why it matters.
